added.name: Evardi
added.long_description: At least 94% of US outage minutes start on the distribution grid, and most utilities are blind between the substation and the meter. Evardi builds a live model of a utility’s network from data it already has, matching every meter to its transformer and using virtual meters to show load and solar on every transformer. On top of that model, our AI agents do the engineering work utilities need at the grid edge: checking switching orders, finding outages after extreme weather and planning for new load from DERs and data centers. Because the model sees every transformer, it will also help utilities decide when new wires are really needed, and how distribution load can free up transmission for new data centers. We’re working with utilities across the globe that together serve over 10 million customers.
added.one_liner: Agents that engineer the grid edge

added.name: Ailit
added.long_description:
Ailit is building the electric energy system for North American freight rail. Our first product, Superwagon, is a battery wagon designed to power existing diesel-electric locomotives, allowing railroads to electrify the fleets they already own.

Superwagon carries swappable battery packs that supply electricity to the locomotive’s existing electric motors. Discharged packs are exchanged for charged ones along the route and recharged off-board, providing operators with limitless range.

We deliver energy as a service, owning and operating the batteries and swapping sites. Railroads pay for energy with no upfront equipment purchase, with pricing set at 20% below today’s diesel cost.

Founded in Stockholm by Christian Lind and Emil Tagesson, our team is now based in San Francisco. We’re building our first full-scale prototype and targeting first deployment in summer 2027.
added.one_liner: Electrifying North American freight rail with swappable batteries.

long_description.before:
Reinventing medicine from lab to drug discovery.
NxtCure CRO- an AI-native, full-stack CRO built to take therapeutics from discovery to market faster.
NxtCure Cancer- the all-in-one mobile platform guiding patients through the cancer journey.
We’re building the operating system for the future of medicine.
long_description.after:
Reinventing medicine from lab to drug discovery.
NxtCure CRO- an AI-native, full-stack CRO built to take therapeutics from discovery to market faster.

About 2 million Americans are diagnosed with cancer every year. Science has never moved faster, new immunotherapies, targeted drugs and cancer vaccines arrive every year. But roughly 90% of cancer drugs fail in clinical trials, and about 80% of trials run late. The breakthroughs exist. The way we test them is stuck in the last century.

NxtCure is building autonomous clinical trials. Before a single patient enrolls, we run the trial thousands of times on digital twins. Each virtual patient is a system of coupled differential equations that track how a drug moves through plasma, tumor and heart, and how the tumor grows, shrinks or fights back. The parameters are fit to real trial data, so every twin behaves like real biology. Across thousands of simulations we can calculate the odds that a dose will hit its endpoints, and fix the protocol before it costs anyone time, money or hope.

Then 13 AI agents run the trial. Each one owns a stage: drafting the protocol, ranking sites, pre-screening patients, forecasting drug supply, watching for adverse events, predicting dropout, cleaning data and writing the final report. As real data comes in, the twins update and flag problems weeks before a human would see them.

In 2025, the FDA laid out how computer simulation can take its place. Soon a cancer drug will run through thousands of simulated trials before it ever touches a lab, and reach patients years faster. We’re building that future.

long_description.after:
Perit is a training-data company for frontier AI labs. Everything we deliver is recorded, transcribed, labelled and graded by people who actually do the job: ex-contact-centre QA leads, claims handlers, ward clerks and shopkeepers, recruited for the sector and locale each program needs.

What we deliver:

- Voice and speech data: 4,000+ hours of audio delivered across 9 locales, transcribed verbatim and word-aligned, with 95%+ QA-sample accuracy.
- RL environments and benchmarks: speech-to-speech RL environments plus coding and RL task sets, currently 100 RL tasks per week and scalable to 2,000.
- Embodied data for robotics: egocentric video, depth, teleoperation and handheld-gripper demonstrations recorded in real homes, shops and workplaces.
- Data collection and annotation: video, image and text collected to spec, and annotation of any data type on our own Foundry workspace.

Every batch ships with a quality report, consent references and a reviewer chain. We work with almost all frontier labs and have quickly gotten past $9M in revenue.

Founded by 2x YC founders Kshitij Dixit (Zeo, YC W20) and Poorva Dixit (ex-Google Cloud AI, Uber, Atlassian), with a deep IIT network of researchers at top labs.

long_description.before:
Ascenix is building custom software for running senior homes. We combine reusable building blocks into workflows tailored to each home's existing processes, from incident reporting to reimbursement. Homes get custom software without hiring an engineering team.

Living in a retirement home convinced us that the best way to improve residents' lives is to improve the systems staff rely on. As the older population grows, care teams need more time and resources. Repetitive reporting, missed reimbursement, and compliance problems take those away, while disconnected tools add costs and leave staff moving information between systems.

Our building blocks gather information from EHRs like PointClickCare and other sources, process it, apply rules, and produce reports, tasks, or emails. Incident reporting and reimbursement reviews usually come from two separate vendors. Ascenix builds both from the same blocks, in one interface, so data isn't stuck in silos. Homes start with their biggest bottleneck and add workflows as priorities change.
